subject: Clarify: microburst rounding / prefix accounting for pilot
messages:
From: Elaine Rivera <elaine@acmecorp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected microburst line-item on last invoice

Hi Vivek,

We noticed a handful of small, high-frequency calls in our November usage that got rounded up to a full 'session' charge in the invoice. Example: 23 separate calls at ~12 tokens each across the same minute ended up billed as three full session minimums. Can you explain how the billing window and rounding logic treated those?

For context: this is our live chat routing (short questions) hitting your hosted API through the pilot. We expected either per-call metering (small fractional tokens) or an explicit microburst smoothing policy; the invoice looked like a bundling of several of those into minimum buckets.

Procurement is concerned because this could materially shift our forecast for the pilot. Can you send a short summary of the rules and whether there's a mitigation we can apply (e.g., heartbeat prefix, warm cache credit, or different SKU)?

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Rivera
CTO, AcmeCorp

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Rivera <elaine@acmecorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected microburst line-item on last invoice

Hi Elaine — thanks for the note and the example. Short answer: what you saw is the interaction of our microburst aggregation window and the billing quantum/minimums we apply to short calls.

High level:
- Calls that occur within a short aggregation window (default 60s for the hosted tier) can be folded into a single billing bucket when they share the same prefix/cache context. That helps in many apps but can cause apparent "round-up" if many tiny calls fall across bucket boundaries.
- We also apply a minimum billable quantum for per-call usage to prevent excessive metering overhead; currently the hosted default quantum is 100 tokens per call unless the workload is covered by a session/commit.

I'm attaching our short playbook that explains the default windows and recommended mitigations. Two immediate options for Acme: a) enable the microburst smoothing pilot (gives a small pool of burst credits and reduces the quantum to 20 tokens for qualifying short calls), or b) switch the short-chat routes to a pinned mini-session SKU (30-minute ephemeral sessions) that amortizes those tiny calls.

I want to loop in Marissa/Ben from billing so we can propose a concrete concession for the pilot while procurement reviews contract language. Can you share a sample of the timestamps for the affected calls (HubSpot record or a CSV)?

Cheers,
Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_billing_playbook_v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Rivera <elaine@acmecorp.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 14:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected microburst line-item on last invoice

Thanks for the details, Elaine. Adding clarity from the billing side so procurement can see the options in writing.

How the math worked (concise):
- Your 23 calls (~12 tokens each) spanned three aggregation windows that were closed by a heartbeat mismatch; we credited prefix reuse within the window but each closed window triggered the minimum quantum.
- Minimum quantum we charged: 100 tokens per call-equivalent. So each closed window rounded to the nearest 100-token slab; multiple small calls that don't align to the same open slot can therefore result in several 100-token charges.

Proposal for concession during the pilot (two items):
1) Microburst smoothing pilot: We will apply a temporary microburst credit pool for ACME that reduces the effective minimum quantum to 20 tokens for qualifying short calls. This will be reconciled monthly and shown as a line-item credit.
2) Usage sample review: We'll run your November calls against an alternate config (ephemeral mini-sessions and/or reduced aggregation window) and show simulated invoice impact.

If procurement wants firm wording, we can add a clause to the SOW that specifies the pilot smoothing terms and a one-time invoice credit if realized usage exceeds the modeled amount.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_proposed_pricing_sheet.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Rivera <elaine@acmecorp.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected microburst line-item on last invoice

Elaine — quick note on packaging that may help with forecast stability. Two concrete commercial options we can offer for the pilot:

A) Commitment + Smoothing Addendum
- Acme commits to a small monthly token commit (e.g., 500k tokens) at a discounted rate.
- We layer a microburst smoothing addendum that creates a shared credit pool for small calls; this prevents per-call quantum rounding for qualifying prefixes.
- Result: predictable monthly spend and fewer surprises.

B) Metered with Threshold Waiver
- Keep metered per-token billing but add a threshold waiver for the pilot months: if the rounding-induced overage exceeds X% of the modeled usage, Redwood issues a one-time invoice credit to true-up.

From an implementation perspective, option A requires a short amendment (billing + SSO mapping), option B can be handled as a one-off credit line with an agreed measurement method. Happy to draft either into the SOW language.

—Ben
VP, Revenue Operations

From: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 11:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected microburst line-item on last invoice

Thanks — Procurement prefers option A for predictability. Two asks before we sign-off on the amendment:
1) Please add a short definition of "microburst smoothing" in the SOW with a sample calculation (how credits are consumed).
2) Example invoice row showing the credit and how it will appear (so we can reconcile).

We will push draft amendment language back to you by Wednesday if you send a template.

Procurement Team
AcmeCorp

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 15:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected microburst line-item on last invoice

Appreciate the quick decision — glad option A works. Action items we agreed on today: 
- Marissa/Ben: send a one-page SOW amendment template that defines microburst smoothing, includes a sample credit consumption calc, and an example invoice row. Target: EOD Wed 2026-12-09 (we have an internal deadline to present to legal).
- Acme: share the usage CSV or HubSpot record for the November sample (Vivek already shared link above).
- Kim: check if the smoothing pilot needs any runtime config change (short aggregation window or new prefix tagging) and confirm the rollout ETA.

I'll follow up with the draft amendment attached to HubSpot when ready. Thanks everyone — looking forward to closing the pilot terms.

Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
